correctness.rationale: Each sphere coordinate is Uniform[-1,1], hence the symmetric node fractions are individually uniform and yield unbiased cell integration. The Taylor expansion at cell midpoint gives leading centered error h^3 f doubleprime(m_i)(V_i^2-1/3)/8 plus uniformly o(h^4) for C^3; the pathwise identity sum_{j=0}^2 (V_j^2-1/3)=0 cancels constant curvature exactly. Across each triple, f doubleprime changes by (j-1)h f tripleprime(c_k), giving leading block error h^4 f tripleprime(c_k)(V_2^2-V_0^2)/8. Uniform S2 squared coordinates have Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2), E V_i^4=1/5, E Vi²Vj²=1/15, so Var(V2²-V0²)=4/15. Independent blocks and Riemann convergence give limit 1/720. Cubic paths make the leading block expression exact, giving a²/(20n^7); quadratic is pathwise exact. Block size 1 impossible by nondegenerate squared uniform; size 2 impossible since P(V1²>2/3)>0 contradicts a fixed squared sum 2/3. Independent exact rational sphere-path and moment checks agree; finite checks do not prove the C3 limit.

value.rationale: The same two evaluations per cell gain two powers in variance decay for smooth integrands through deliberate dependence while preserving unbiasedness and giving pathwise quadratic precision. The minimal three-cell coupling size is a sharp structural lower bound, and the constant 1/720 is an independently meaningful numerical-analysis invariant.

final_claim: On uniform n-cell grids, 3|n, grouping symmetric randomized two-point trapezoids by independent uniform S^2 coordinate triples makes quadrature pathwise exact for every quadratic and unbiased for continuous f; for real C^3 f, n^7 Var(Q_n) -> integral_0^1 (f triple prime)^2/720; exact cubic variance a^2/(20n^7). Three is the minimal block size with individual uniform sampling fractions; IID cells instead have n^5 variance limit integral(f double prime)^2/720.
limitations: Requires uniform n divisible 3, independent sphere blocks and deterministic real C3 integrands; no minimax or rough-input claim.
residual_risks: Specialized dependent-stratified randomized quadrature work could contain the same three-block method.
Not an optimality theorem among all couplings or rough integrands.
